# ocr

Imported as `@elffuss/ai/ocr`, `@elffuss/ai/ocr/sizes`.

## `sdk/ocr/config.js`

The settings of the two PP-OCR models, read from their own inference.yml (the files the registry pins), so the pipeline follows the model and not a copy of its numbers: thresholds and normalisation of the detector, input height of the recogniser. A small YAML reader covers what those files use: block mappings and sequences, nested sequences, quoted and plain scalars, anchors and aliases.

### `yamlTrim`

Trim the two characters YAML treats as white space (space and tab), nothing else.

### `yamlScalar(raw)`

Value of one YAML scalar as written (quoted or plain).

### `unescapeDouble(s)`

The escapes of a YAML double-quoted scalar.

### `parseYaml(text)`

Parse the YAML subset of the PaddleOCR inference files.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` |  |

Returns `any`.

### `parseDetConfig(yml)`

Detection settings of a PP-OCR det model (its inference.yml).
The resize rule is not in the file: the shortest side is brought up to 736,
the longest kept under 4000 (the model's own largest input), both sides
rounded to multiples of 32.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `yml` | `string` |  |

### `parseScale(v)`

`1./255.` and the like, without evaluating anything.

### `parseRecConfig(yml)`

Recognition settings of a PP-OCR rec model (its inference.yml): input
height and base width, channel order, and the decoder it was trained for.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `yml` | `string` |  |

## `sdk/ocr/crop.js`

One detected quadrilateral → an upright strip of pixels for the recogniser, as PaddleOCR's get_rotate_crop_image does it: the size is the longer of each pair of opposite sides, the quadrilateral is mapped onto it with a perspective transform and bicubic sampling (edges repeated), and a strip at least 1.5 times taller than wide is turned a quarter to the left, because vertical text reads that way. Plain arithmetic: no canvas, so every browser and backend gets the same pixels.

### `perspective(from, to)`

The perspective transform that maps the four `from` points onto the four `to` points.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | `number[][]` |  |
| `to` | `number[][]` |  |

Returns `Float64Array`: 3 × 3, row-major, last element 1

### `solve(A, b)`

Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting. Throws on a singular system.

### `cubicWeights(t, out = new Float64Array(4))`

Cubic convolution weights for a fractional offset (a = −0.75, as OpenCV).

### `cropQuad(img, quad)`

Crop a quadrilateral (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left) out of
RGBA pixels into an RGB strip.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `img` | `{ width: number, height: number, data: Uint8ClampedArray\|Uint8Array }` | RGBA |
| `quad` | `number[][]` |  |

Returns `{ width: number, height: number, data: Uint8Array, rotated: boolean } \| null`.

### `rotateLeft({ width: w, height: h, data })`

Turn an RGB strip a quarter to the left (numpy's rot90 with k = 1).

## `sdk/ocr/det.js`

Text detection around the PP-OCR DB detector: the resize of the input (sides in multiples of 32, the shortest brought up to a minimum, the longest kept under the model's limit), the normalised BGR tensor, and the post-processing of its probability map into quadrilaterals. The post-processing follows the DB post-processing of PaddleOCR (https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR, Apache-2.0): threshold, connected regions, minimum-area rectangle, mean probability inside it, expansion by area × ratio / perimeter, and scaling back to the image. Everything here is plain arithmetic on typed arrays.

### `detInputSize(width, height, { limitSideLen, maxSideLimit, multiple })`

Size of the detector input for an image.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `width` | `number` |  |
| `height` | `number` |  |
| `cfg` | `{ limitSideLen: number, maxSideLimit: number, multiple: number }` |  |

Returns `{ width: number, height: number }`.

### `detTensor(img, outW, outH, { mean, std, scale, bgr })`

Bilinear resample of RGBA pixels (pixel centres aligned, edges clamped), one
channel at a time into a planar float tensor, normalised per channel.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `img` | `{ width: number, height: number, data: Uint8ClampedArray\|Uint8Array }` | RGBA |
| `outW` | `number` |  |
| `outH` | `number` |  |
| `norm` | `{ mean: readonly number[], std: readonly number[], scale: number, bgr: boolean }` |  |

Returns `Float32Array`: 3 × outH × outW, channel order B, G, R when `bgr`

### `regions(prob, width, height, thresh)`

Connected regions (8-connected) of the pixels above `thresh`, by runs.
Each region comes with the end points of its runs (enough for its convex
hull) and its bounding box, in raster order of their first pixel.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `prob` | `Float32Array` | height × width |

Returns `{ points: Int32Array, count: number, xmin: number, ymin: number, xmax: number, ymax: number }[]`.

### `convexHull(flat, count = flat.length / 2)`

Convex hull (monotone chain) of points given as [x0, y0, x1, y1, …].

Returns `number[][]`: counter clockwise in image coordinates, no repeated end

### `minAreaRect(hull)`

Minimum-area enclosing rectangle of a convex polygon (each edge tried as a side).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `hull` | `number[][]` |  |

Returns `{ corners: number[][], width: number, height: number }`: `width` along the chosen side

### `miniBoxOrder(corners)`

Order four corners the way PaddleOCR's get_mini_boxes does: top-left,
top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, from the two leftmost and the two
rightmost points.

### `boxScore(prob, width, height, quad)`

Mean of `prob` inside a convex quadrilateral, over the pixels whose centre it covers.

### `rowSpan(poly, y)`

Horizontal extent [x0, x1] of a convex polygon at height y, or null.

### `unclipRect(rect, ratio)`

Grow a rectangle by d = area × ratio / perimeter on every side, which is
what offsetting it with round joins and taking the minimum-area rectangle
of the result gives.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `rect` | `{ corners: number[][], width: number, height: number }` |  |

### `orderClockwise(pts)`

Corners clockwise from the top-left as PaddleOCR orders them before cropping:
smallest and largest x + y, then the other two by y − x.

### `dbPostprocess(prob, width, height, cfg, destWidth, destHeight)`

Probability map → text quadrilaterals in image pixels.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `prob` | `Float32Array` | height × width map of the detector |
| `width` | `number` | map width (the detector input) |
| `height` | `number` | map height |
| `cfg` | `{ thresh: number, boxThresh: number, maxCandidates: number, unclipRatio: number, minSize: number }` |  |
| `destWidth` | `number` | image width |
| `destHeight` | `number` | image height |

Returns `{ points: number[][], score: number }[]`.

### `filterBoxes(boxes, width, height)`

What PaddleOCR keeps of the detections before cropping: corners in clockwise
order, clipped to the image, and only boxes more than 3 pixels each way.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `boxes` | `{ points: number[][], score: number }[]` |  |

## `sdk/ocr/dict.js`

The characters a PP-OCR recogniser can write, in the order of its output classes. The CTC head has one class per character plus a blank before them and a space after them, so a model whose last dimension is not the list length plus two is not the model this list belongs to.

## `sdk/ocr/impl.js`

The OCR task where the model runs (a Worker): PP-OCR detection and recognition used directly with ONNX Runtime Web. Both models and both settings files come from the store through the task context, checked against the registry; the dictionary and the decoder are checked against the recogniser's outputs before anything is read. No fetch, no DOM.

## `sdk/ocr/index.js`

@elffuss/ai/ocr: read the text of an image, in the browser. PP-OCR (PaddleOCR, Apache-2.0) detection and recognition with ONNX Runtime Web, on WebGPU or WebAssembly; the model comes from the Elffuss model store at a pinned revision. Spanish and English, and every other language of its Latin and Chinese character list.

### Type `OcrBox`

```ts
{ xmin: number, ymin: number, xmax: number, ymax: number }
```

Axis-aligned box of a line, in pixels of the input.

### Type `OcrLine`

```ts
{ text: string, score: number, box: OcrBox, polygon: number[][] }
```

One line of text: what it says, the recogniser's mean confidence (0-1), its box, and its four corners (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left).

### Type `OcrResult`

```ts
{ text: string, lines: OcrLine[], width: number, height: number, device: 'webgpu'|'wasm' }
```

The page text (rows top to bottom, a row's lines joined with a space), the lines in reading order, the input's size and the backend that read it.

### Type `OcrRunOptions`

```ts
{ signal?: AbortSignal, maxSide?: number, minScore?: number }
```

`maxSide` scales a larger input down before reading it (at most 4000, the detector's limit; boxes are still given in the input's pixels); `minScore` drops lines the recogniser is less sure of (0.5 by default).

### `ocr`

Read one image: load, run once, dispose. Options of the task (`device`,
`onProgress`, `signal`…) and of the run (`maxSide`, `minScore`) in one object.

## `sdk/ocr/order.js`

Reading order of the lines of one page, and the text made from them. Boxes whose vertical extents overlap by more than half the smaller height share a row; rows go from top to bottom and the boxes of a row from left to right. The boxes of a row are joined with a space and the rows with a line break. Plus the helpers to compare a text with a reference: normalisation (NFC, single spaces, trimmed lines) and the character error rate.

### `boundingBox(points)`

Axis-aligned box of a polygon.

### `readingRows(lines)`

Group lines into rows and order them.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `lines` | `L[]` |  |

Returns `L[][]`: rows , top to bottom, each left to right

### `cleanLine(s)`

One line of recognised text: trimmed, spaces collapsed.

### `pageText(lines)`

The lines in reading order and the page text.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `lines` | `L[]` |  |

Returns `{ lines: L[], text: string }`.

### `normalizeText(s)`

NFC, runs of spaces as one, every line trimmed, no empty lines at the ends.

### `characterErrorRate(hypothesis, reference)`

Character error rate: edit distance between two texts (by code point) over
the length of the reference. Both are normalised first.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `hypothesis` | `string` |  |
| `reference` | `string` |  |

The OCR of one page, from RGBA pixels to lines of text with their boxes: detect, post-process, crop, recognise in batches, decode, order. The two sessions come from outside (ONNX Runtime, any backend), so this module runs the same in a Worker, on a page or in Node.

## `sdk/ocr/rec.js`

Text recognition around the PP-OCR CTC recogniser: strips are grouped by shape into batches, each strip is resized to the model's height keeping its shape (padded on the right up to the batch width, at least 320 at height 48), normalised to [−1, 1] in BGR order, and the output classes are read with greedy CTC decoding: the best class at each step, repeats merged, blanks dropped, and the mean probability of what is kept as the score. This follows the recognition pre-processing and CTCLabelDecode of PaddleOCR (https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR, Apache-2.0).

### `batchWidth(strips, { height, width, maxWidth })`

Width of a batch: the model's base width, or wider for the widest strip of
the batch, never more than `maxWidth`.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `strips` | `{ width: number, height: number }[]` |  |
| `cfg` | `{ height: number, width: number, maxWidth: number }` |  |

### `stripWidth(strip, imgW, height)`

Width a strip takes inside a batch of width `imgW`.

### `planBatches(strips, cfg, { maxBatch = 6, maxSteps = 640 } = {})`

Batches of strip indices, narrowest shape first, bounded in count and in
total output steps (each step is a row of every class of the model).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `strips` | `{ width: number, height: number }[]` |  |
| `cfg` | `{ height: number, width: number, maxWidth: number }` |  |
| `[limits]` | `{ maxBatch?: number, maxSteps?: number }` |  |

Returns `number[][]`.

### `writeStrip(tensor, b, imgW, strip, { height, bgr })`

Write one strip into slot `b` of a batch tensor (B × 3 × height × imgW,
zero-filled): bilinear resize to `height` rows and its own width, rounded to
bytes like an 8-bit image, then (v / 255 − 0.5) / 0.5.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `tensor` | `Float32Array` |  |
| `b` | `number` |  |
| `imgW` | `number` |  |
| `strip` | `{ width: number, height: number, data: Uint8Array }` | RGB |
| `cfg` | `{ height: number, bgr: boolean }` |  |

### `ctcDecode(probs, B, T, C, vocab)`

Greedy CTC decoding of a B × T × C block of class probabilities.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `probs` | `Float32Array` |  |
| `B` | `number` |  |
| `T` | `number` |  |
| `C` | `number` |  |
| `vocab` | `string[]` | index 0 is the blank |

Returns `{ text: string, score: number }[]`.
